segmenti.tekst: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين

wa sallama tasliman kathiran ila yawm id-din. Qalallahu fi kitabihi al-karim: “Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu ittaqullaha haqqa tuqatihi wa la tamutunna illa wa antum muslimun.” Amma ba'd. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his

companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Dear brothers, respected congregation, know that in a person there is an organ, a lump: if it is sound, the body will be sound; if it is diseased, the person's body will be diseased – and that is the heart.

These are the words of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. In order for a person to keep his heart sound, for his heart to be pure, he must know, or it is necessary for him to know, the things that destroy that heart or make it sick.
Ibn al-Qayyim, rahimahullahu ta'ala (may Allah have mercy on him), says: there are five things that destroy a person's heart. Five things. What does Ibn al-Qayyim mention in first place?

“Kathrat al-mukhalatah” – excessive socializing. See how precise Ibn al-Qayyim was? He did not say socializing, but excessive socializing. That a person is in constant contact with people. As we would say: idle coffee drinking. Idle coffee drinking. Especially when the company is bad. When the company is bad. What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say: “A man is upon the religion of his friend.”

So be very careful with whom you… with whom you go out, with whom you spend time, and so on, and so on, and so forth. How many brotherly relationships has this excessive socializing destroyed? How many brotherly relationships has it destroyed? How much livelihood, how many families has it destroyed? Why, dear brothers?

Because that excessive socializing leads a person to burden himself with other people's problems. Not only does he burden himself with other people's problems, not only that, but, unfortunately, dear brothers, when people are idle, two will not meet without backbiting a third, without backbiting a third.

We have people – he finishes work, and what does he do, what does he get up to? The first thing is, he calls for coffee. Then from coffee to coffee, from coffee to coffee, and there it is, time for isha.

After isha, again from coffee to coffee. Where is your time for the Lord? Where is your time for worship? Where is your time for your family? There is none, there is none. And when you invite him to the mosque, he says: “By Allah, I don't have time.

I'm killing myself with work.” Killing himself with work. As we said, especially when, when the company is bad. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an? He says: and when the disbeliever says, when a person will bite his fingers out of fear, his nails – what does he say?

He says: “Woe to me, if only,” he says, “I had not…” He says: “Woe to me, if only I had held to the right path, if only I had held to the path of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Woe to me, if only I had not taken so-and-so…”

As what, dear brothers? As friends. As friends. A person will flee from his friend, from the one… of course, from the one who led him away from the right path. And you know the uncle, Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

The Prophet comes to him before his death, so that he would pronounce “La ilaha illallah”; Abu Jahl and the rest of the company come to him and say: “Remain on the religion of your forefathers.” What happens? The man, because of bad company, says: “I remain on the religion of my forefathers,” and he dies as a disbeliever, as a polytheist. That is bad company.

And in everything in which a person goes to excess, that is not good, it is not good, it is not good for a person. The second thing Ibn al-Qayyim mentions, he says: sailing the sea of vain desires, daydreams, daydreams.

There are people who daydream their whole life, or their entire life, about being rich, about being [unclear], about having women, and so on and so forth. And his whole life passes in that. There are those who daydream so much that they think there is no one more beautiful than them, that no one deserves them.

And so he daydreams about some princess, or the other way around, a girl waits for some prince on a white horse, she turns 25, 30, 35, 40 – the years pass. A person should not live in fantasy, should not live in fantasy, but should live in the real world.
We should dream about how to improve ourselves in a positive sense. A person cannot dream of being rich, fold his hands behind his head, lie down on the bed, and do nothing about it.

That is, you are killing yourself. When you wake up from the fantasy, then it often happens that a person becomes disappointed with life. He becomes disappointed with life. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say: “Ya'iduhum wa yumannihim” – He says: Satan makes promises to them, gives people false promises – “wa yumannihim” – and false fantasies, false fantasies, so that people daydream. “وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا” – and, He says, Satan promises them nothing

but deception, nothing but false promises, and a person becomes disappointed with life. That is why a person should live in reality. If you dream of memorizing the Qur'an, you sit down and memorize the Qur'an. If you dream of building a house, you [unclear], you work, you build a house. The third thing that Ibn al-Qayyim mentions is at the same time the most dangerous of the things we have mentioned and will mention.

It is attaching the heart to someone other than Allah. Which is at the same time, dear brothers, disbelief. Which means it is also disbelief. Attaching… We have, that is, many, many false deities today that people, people worship; especially in the time of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, there was a lot of that. And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا” – and He says: they took deities so that they would be a source of strength for them.

“Kalla” – He says, it is not so. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “Sa yakfuruna bi 'ibadatihim” – He says: those false deities will deny the worship of these people on the Day of Judgment and will be against them, they will be their enemies on the Day of Judgment.

Also included here, dear brothers, is when a person loves something more, besides Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. When he loves something, that is, when he loves something more than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, whether it be children, wife, money, and so on.
We said a little earlier: a person feels such love for money that he cannot leave work to pray. “I can't,” he says, “I don't have time.” A person has no time for the One who created time, imagine.
A person does not have time, out of 24 hours, to set aside an hour for the Lord of all the worlds, the One who created him, who gave him his sustenance.

A person should think carefully about these things. The fourth thing that Ibn al-Qayyim, rahimahullah, mentions is, he says, “kathrat at-ta'am”: that a person eats a lot of food, that he consumes a lot of food.

Excessive consumption of food causes the heart to weaken. You know, when a person eats his fill – that is, we all know – sleepiness immediately comes. And that deadens a person, deadens his heart, his soul.

What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an? “وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا” – and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say: one third of one's stomach for food, one third for water, and let the third remain empty, so that a person can be active.
What do we do today? We put two thirds for food, one for water, and that's it. One… afterwards a person cannot function properly. Then, what do the scholars say?

The person who eats correctly, properly, they say, is close to the angels. Why? Because the angels neither eat nor drink. And, they say, the one who consumes a lot of food is close to the animals. Because however much food you give an animal, it will eat it.

And the fifth thing Ibn al-Qayyim mentions, he says: that a person sleeps a lot. It is enough for a person to sleep 7 hours, 8 hours a day. Today somehow everything has turned upside down, so people don't sleep until fajr. And why they don't sleep until fajr – rather, they won't pray fajr, so they fall asleep and he wakes up at 3, 4, 5 o'clock.

He wakes up at 3, 4, 5 o'clock and says: “Wallahi, I'm not feeling well somehow, I'm not feeling well.” Of course you won't feel well, when you have no limit in sleeping, neither for the body nor for worship.

Especially, dear brothers, when a person sleeps at fajr time, does not pray fajr, especially when he does not pray fajr in congregation. You know, dear brothers, that prayer in congregation is for men.
Prayer in congregation is prescribed for men. Women pray at home. And imagine, a man neither comes to the mosque nor prays at home, but sleeps.

And he wants his sustenance to come to him. And he wants to have sustenance. But sustenance is distributed at the time of fajr and after fajr. That is how a person should look at these things, think carefully about these things, so that his heart does not become sick.

Because just as the body has its food, so too the soul needs you to give it its food. The soul too needs, needs food. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among His good, sincere servants, those who fall into prostration only to Him.
I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us the sins of our parents, to admit us into Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله لي ولكم فاستغفروه إنه هو الغفور الرحيم
